intro.title: Primitive Types & Variable Annotations
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that stores and displays different kinds of basic data, like a user's name, age, and membership status. You will learn about primitive types, which are the fundamental building blocks of data in TypeScript, such as strings, numbers, and booleans. The core concept is variable annotation, where you explicitly tell TypeScript what type of data a variable should hold to make your code more predictable and catch errors early. You will use TypeScript's syntax to declare variables with types like `string`, `number`, and `boolean`. This practice helps you write clearer, more reliable code as a beginner.
intro.usecase: Primitive types and variable annotations are foundational in real-world TypeScript applications like e-commerce platforms, where product prices are stored as numbers, product names as strings, and availability status as booleans. In user dashboards, variables track user IDs (numbers), usernames (strings), and subscription status (booleans) to display personalized content. Form validation systems rely on typed variables to ensure email addresses are strings, quantities are numbers, and checkbox selections are booleans before processing submissions. This type safety prevents runtime errors in critical features like shopping carts, user authentication, and data filtering interfaces.
